results.system_description: Varbench Heisenberg/chain_20_O: spin-1/2 Heisenberg model, Pauli convention, J = 1
results.source_location: Varbench data release, file Heisenberg/chain_20_O.md, row "RNN" (commit 390a21e)
results.eligibility_evidence: Energy of a neural-network state optimized and evaluated with variational Monte Carlo (NetKet) by the Varbench authors and published with arXiv:2302.04919; columns Energy, Sigma (statistical error) and Energy Variance. Script: https://github.com/varbench/methods/blob/main/scripts/Heisenberg/chain_20_O/vmc_rnn.sh
results.notes: Varbench defines the Heisenberg model with Pauli matrices, H = J sum sigma_i · sigma_j (NetKet's Heisenberg operator); this instance uses S = sigma/2, so the printed energy and error bar are multiplied by convention_factor 0.25 and the variance by 0.0625. The RNN script does not fix the magnetization; the ground state of the even chain is a singlet with total Sz = 0.

results.source_location: Varbench data release, file TFIsing/chain_32_P_1.md, row "RBM (alpha = 1)" (commit 390a21e)
results.eligibility_evidence: Energy of a neural-network state optimized and evaluated with variational Monte Carlo (NetKet) by the Varbench authors and published with arXiv:2302.04919; columns Energy, Sigma (statistical error) and Energy Variance. Script: https://github.com/varbench/methods/blob/main/scripts/TFIsing/chain_32_P_1/vmc_rbm.sh
results.notes: Varbench writes H = J sum sigma^z sigma^z + Gamma sum sigma^x; the NetKet script uses IsingJax with J = -1, which is this instance's Hamiltonian. On the even ring the two are related by flipping every other spin and a global rotation, with the same spectrum, so no factor is needed.

results.source_location: Varbench data release, file Heisenberg/pyrochlore-2x2x2_32_P.md, row "RBM with symmetry projections" (commit 390a21e)
results.eligibility_evidence: Energy of a symmetry-projected RBM neural-network state evaluated by VMC, published in the Varbench data with columns Energy, Sigma (statistical error) and Energy Variance. Varbench credits arXiv:2101.08787, whose appendix (Appendix on NQS) says an RBM with symmetry projectors was used to improve the CNN results on the 4 x 2^3 cluster.
results.notes: Varbench defines the Heisenberg model with Pauli matrices, H = J sum sigma_i · sigma_j; this instance uses S = sigma/2, so the printed energy and error bar are multiplied by convention_factor 0.25 and the variance by 0.0625. This number is not printed in arXiv:2101.08787, whose table gives the CNN value -0.5128(1) per site for this cluster; it is recorded from the Varbench data, where it was first published.

results.eligibility_evidence: Energy of a neural-network state optimized and evaluated with variational Monte Carlo (NetKet) by the Varbench authors and published with arXiv:2302.04919; columns Energy, Sigma (statistical error) and Energy Variance. Script: https://github.com/varbench/methods/blob/main/scripts/TFIsing/chain_32_P_1/vmc_gcnn.sh
results.notes: Varbench writes H = J sum sigma^z sigma^z + Gamma sum sigma^x; the NetKet script uses IsingJax with J = -1, which is this instance's Hamiltonian. On the even ring the two are related by flipping every other spin and a global rotation, with the same spectrum, so no factor is needed. The script (varbench/methods at ed31bb0) runs vmc.py --net gcnn --layers 2 --features 32, a translation-equivariant group-convolutional network. Above the exact energy in the same file.
